title_en: Method in the Seeking of Knowledge
body_ar:
العلم خير ما تفنى فيه الأعمار، وأفضل ما يتنافس فيه الأبرار، ولذلك جعل الله للعلماء منزلة سامقة، ومكانة عالية، وأكرمهم بما لم يكرم به غيرهم، ولطالب العلم آداب وأركان وأجنحة ينبغي له معرفتها ومراعاتها في حال طلبه وانشغاله بالعلم، كما أن عليه أن يهتم بترتيب الأولويات، وتقديم الأهم على المهم.
فضل العلم والعلماء:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه، ومن اهتدى بهديه، واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته. أما بعد: فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى عظم شأن العلم، فأشهد العلماء على أعظم شهادة بعد أن شهد بها وأشهد بها ملائكته، فقال تعالى: شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلائِكَةُ وَأُوْلُوا الْعِلْمِ [آل عمران:18] . وحكم بفضلهم على من سواهم، فقال: قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ وَالَّذِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ [الزمر:9]...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* Knowledge is the best thing in which lifetimes are spent, and the best thing in which the righteous compete. For this reason God appointed for the scholars a towering rank and a high standing, and honoured them with what He did not honour others with. The student of knowledge has proprieties, essential elements and wings which he ought to know and to observe while he is seeking and occupied with knowledge; and he must likewise concern himself with the ordering of priorities, and with putting what is more important before what is important.

## The merit of knowledge and of the scholars

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and God's mercy and His blessings. To proceed: God, glorified and exalted is He, magnified the standing of knowledge, and had the scholars bear witness to the greatest testimony of all, after He had borne witness to it Himself and had His angels bear witness to it. He, exalted is He, said: {God bears witness that there is no god but He, and so do the angels and those possessed of knowledge} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:18). And He judged them to be more excellent than everyone else, and said: {Say: are those who know and those who do not know equal?} (Sūrat al-Zumar 39:9) …

flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis after the second proof-text, so that the method of the title, the proprieties of the student, and the ordering of priorities are all announced by the synopsis and none of them is reached. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/g-19.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلائِكَةُ وَأُوْلُوا الْعِلْمِ [آل عمران:18]
flags.context: the first proof-text, against the same verse as cited in record 726 of this run
options: reproduce the shortened citation as served and record the difference
complete the verse from the received text
flags.note: Style guide section 11, the scripture-lacuna rule. The same verse is cited in record 726 of this same run in full, continuing 'قائماً بالقسط لا إله إلا هو العزيز الحكيم'; here it stops at 'وأولوا العلم' with no ellipsis marking the break. That is consistent with a speaker citing only as far as he needs, but it leaves the English quotation ending mid-verse. Nothing has been restored. The English closes the braces where the Arabic closes and the reference is given as the source gives it.

The third noun is the difficulty. 'أجنحة', wings, is a live metaphor in the literature on seeking knowledge — the things that carry a student, as against the 'أركان' that hold him up — and the English keeps the image rather than flattening it to 'aids', because the metaphor is what makes the triplet cohere. 'أركان' is rendered 'essential elements' per the glossary, whose omission invalidates, rather than 'pillars'. 'آداب' is 'proprieties', consistently with records 700 and 719.

options: putting what is more important before what is important
giving precedence to the most important over the important
prioritising the essential over the merely useful
flags.note: A fixed formula of the literature on priorities (fiqh al-awlawiyyāt), built on the comparative of a single root. The point is that the choice is between two goods, not between a good and a lesser thing, so the third option is wrong even though it reads more naturally in English. The comparative is kept.

flags.context: the Sheikh's gloss introducing Sūrat al-Zumar 39:9
options: He judged them to be more excellent than everyone else
He decreed their superiority over all others
He ruled that they have merit above all besides them
flags.note: 'حكم' here is God judging or determining, not issuing a legal ruling, and the English avoids 'ruled' for that reason. Note that the verse cited is a rhetorical question and the gloss states its answer; the gloss is the Sheikh's and is kept in his sentence rather than inside the quotation.

translator_notes: One of a run of nine records, IDs 725-733, in the Islamic-thought section, all uploaded on 10 May 2011 within about twenty minutes of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lecture, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/g-* series, numbered g-16 to g-24 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lecture was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.
Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

This record and record 726 of the same run open with the same argument and the same first proof-text, and both break off at the same stage. They appear to be two lectures on closely related subjects, and the site's synopses differ; neither is a duplicate of the other.

The transcribed portion includes the spoken greeting 'السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته' after the opening formula, which is absent from most records in this run and marks it as delivered before an audience. Rendered in full.
No ruling term from the five-rulings table appears anywhere in the record.
